oss.readme:
Craft Anything

  English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 한국어

  See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
  Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
  has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.

  
  
  
  

  

  Download Craft Anything ·
  ArtCraft ·
  All Crafting Apps

  
  
  A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE]
> **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers,
> filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil
> last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

  How it works ·
  Two ways to use it ·
  AI ·
  Agents ·
  Under the hood ·
  Get started ·
  Status ·
  Downloads ·
  Discord

  
    
      🔍 Study anything
      Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.
    
    
      🛠️ Build your own
      Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.
    
    
      ✅ Checked, not guessed
      Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.
    
    
      🤖 Agent-ready
      320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.
    
  

## How it works

Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps,
asking you in plain words when a decision is yours:

1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs.
2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your
   request names (or a sensible default).
3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet.
4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

  
    
      
      Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
    
    
      
      Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
    
  

## Two ways to use it

- **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it,
  press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the
  agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and
  buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom.
  "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode).
- **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C,
  disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console.

Both modes drive the same engine.

## Clean room or Deep

- **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page
  source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor
  sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened)
  and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused
  and say how to turn on Deep mode.
- **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the
  built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start
  page watched, and the builder may use all of them.

Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with
`--deep` (or `--clean-room`).

  
  
  Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI

Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft
Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything
never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with
Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter
exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed
Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI,
Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki) can be switched to it per backend; of those, only Maki has
been run live. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter and local
OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI).

## Built for agents

Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a
whole rebuild without the app:

```sh
craft-anything-cli commands                                   # every tool, by toolset
craft-anything-cli mcp                                        # serve them to any MCP client
craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website"
```

Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back
as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup`
connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps.

## Under the hood

A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 320 tools (300 in the engine, the rest from the AI and
setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites,
firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and
decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's

oss.readme:
# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)

  DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。

下载 DSH Go

  感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh

## 可以做什么

DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。

- **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。
- **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。
- **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。
- **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。
- **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。
- **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。

功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。

## 安装

安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。

1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。
2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。
3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。

仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。

“发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。

## 常见问题

和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？

没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。

安全吗？

本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。

切到后台会被杀吗？

部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。

对手机有什么要求？

Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。

开源吗？

开源，代码就在这个仓库，以 [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) 发布，`sdk/` 和 `examples/` 为 MIT。DSH Go 的名称和标识，以及 Deepy、鲸娘两位吉祥物，不在开源授权范围内，见 [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md)。再发布和 fork 时的署名要求见[授权范围与再发布](#授权范围与再发布)。

## 从源码构建

以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。

先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git
cd dsh-go

bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh
source tooling/env.sh
flutter --version
java -version

bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon
```

工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。

产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。

构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时：

```bash
bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon
```

未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。

只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行：

```bash
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all
```

## 目录

| 路径 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `app/` | Flutter 界面与 Android Kotlin 平台实现 |
| `packages/dsh_client/` | DSH Web API 的 Dart 客户端 |
| `packages/dsh_remote/` | DSH Remote 的 Dart 客户端 |
| `runtime/` | Linux 运行时打包、引擎补丁与 App 桥接 |
| `sdk/plugin-kit/` | 原生插件作者工具包；在仓库中使用，未发布到 npm |
| `examples/plugins/` | 插件示例 |
| `docs/guide/`、`docs/plugins/` | 用户指南与插件开发文档 |
| `docs/assets/` | 本页用到的展示图、桌宠动图和社群二维码 |
| `tooling/` | 工具链、APK 构建与诊断脚本 |
| `services/`、`site/`、`infra/` | 配套分享服务、网站和部署材料 |

## 参与贡献

问题反馈和改进建议可提交到 [Issues](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/issues)。代码、文档和翻译贡献请先看 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。插件作者可以从[插件教程](docs/plugins/README.md)和 [SDK](sdk/plugin-kit/README.md)开始。

安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 报告，避免在公开 Issue 中提交漏洞细节或凭据。

oss.readme:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

oss.description: Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it for 20/30/40 series cards. Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput
oss.readme:
![gpu-unlock: full-speed tensor cores for GeForce RTX](assets/banner.svg)

### Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it.

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-76b900)![RTX 20 | 30 | 40](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-RTX%2020%20%7C%2030%20%7C%2040-76b900?logo=nvidia&logoColor=white)![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux-informational?logo=linux&logoColor=white)![License GPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Zagitta/gpu-unlock?style=flat&color=yellow)

**Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput** · **+25–55% LLM prefill** · **+25–50% fine-tuning** · **+30–55% image generation**

[Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus) · [Benchmarks](#what-you-get) · [Install](#how-to-install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Support](#support-me)

---

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

---

## What you get

The tensor core rate doubles. How much of that you see depends on how much of
your workload is FP16/BF16/TF32 matrix math, and on whether the card has the
power headroom to run it.

Dense matrix multiply (FP32 accumulation, stock power limits):

| Card | BF16 before | BF16 after | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12 GB | 27 TFLOPS | 51 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 3060 Ti | 37 TFLOPS | 68 TFLOPS | +82% |
| RTX 3070 | 40 TFLOPS | 72 TFLOPS | +81% |
| RTX 3080 10 GB | 65 TFLOPS | 113 TFLOPS | +73% |
| RTX 3090 | 75 TFLOPS | 125 TFLOPS | +65% |
| RTX 3090 Ti (450 W) | 88 TFLOPS | 157 TFLOPS | +80% |
| RTX 4070 Ti | 81 TFLOPS | 150 TFLOPS | +84% |
| RTX 4080 | 104 TFLOPS | 193 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 4090 | 165 TFLOPS | 329 TFLOPS | +100% (peak MMA rate) |

The RTX 4090 runs out of power before it runs out of tensor cores, so large
GEMMs at stock power limits gain much less than the peak rate suggests.

Real workloads:

| Workload | Typical speedup |
| --- | --- |
| LLM prefill / prompt processing, FP16/BF16 or AWQ/GPTQ (vLLM, PyTorch, Transformers) | +25–55% |
| Time to first token | 25–30% lower |
| LoRA and full fine-tuning in BF16 | +25–50% |
| Image generation, FP16/BF16 (SDXL, SD 1.5, Krea, DiT models in ComfyUI) | +30–55% |
| Video generation, BF16 compute (Wan 2.2) | +15–20% |
| FlashAttention / SDPA kernels | +50–60% |
| llama.cpp / Ollama with quantized GGUF | 0–15%, mostly at long context |
| LLM decode / token generation (memory bound) | No change |
| INT8, FP8 and INT4 models | No change |
| Gaming and FP32 CUDA | No change |

Outputs are bit-identical before and after; only the speed changes. These
numbers come from the [compatibility reports](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues)
users have filed, where you can find full benchmark details and post your own.

---

## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping
existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`
in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run
`sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run
`sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.
- **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in your boot entry
(`bootctl status` shows its location).
- **UKI / generated entries:** add it to `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and regenerate
your boot images/entries (e.g. `sudo mkinitcpio -P` for mkinitcpio UKIs).

# FAQ

- Q: Do you have a website/coin/installer?  
A: No this is the one and only OG source for gpu-unlock. Crypto, websites, installers and what else is not associated with this project or the developer in any way shape or form. 
- Q: Does this depend on a specific driver version? I see `610.43.03` is pinned.  
A: No the driver is only fetched to extract firmware this unlock depends on    
- Q: What about Windows?  
A: I don't run windows and don't plan to maintain it but [https://github.com/impacifist/Windows-GPU-UNLOCK](https://gi

## Start here

| You have | Go to |
|---|---|
| **An Android TV or Google TV** | [Quick start](#quick-start): a coding assistant does the work in about fifteen minutes. |
| **A Samsung, LG, Roku, Vizio or Hisense VIDAA TV** | [cleanyour.tv/not-android](https://cleanyour.tv/not-android): CleanYourTV can't run there, but you can turn off the tracking with your remote. |
| **A phone or laptop, no coding agent** | One of the [community apps](https://cleanyour.tv/app) for Android phones, Mac and Windows, made by independent developers. |
| **Want to see it first** | [What you get](#what-you-get): screenshots of the new home screen. |

**Official links:** [cleanyour.tv](https://cleanyour.tv) and this repo. Other domains using the name, such as
cleanyourtv.com, are not run by this project ([#1004](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/issues/1004)).
CleanYourTV publishes no app in any app store, and clean-your-tv.net is not ours either.

[How it works](#how-it-works) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [What you get](#what-you-get) ·
[Supported TVs](#supported-tvs) · [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) · [The launcher](#the-launcher) ·
[Restoring](#restoring-your-tv) · [Firmware updates](#after-a-firmware-update) ·
[Questions](#questions-people-ask) · [Contributing](#contributing)

## How it works

Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's
developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling:

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Back up** | The list of installed packages and settings. |
| **Disable** | The manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk, with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. |
| **Install** | A small native launcher, made the default home screen. |

**No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.**

The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask
before touching anything you might use.

## Quick start

| You have | Do this |
|---|---|
| **A computer** | Use the prompt with a coding assistant: the three steps below. |
| **A computer, no coding assistant** | Run the three steps yourself: the commands are in [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand). |
| **A phone or laptop, no coding assistant** | Pick one of the [community apps](https://cleanyour.tv/app): free, open-source apps built on these TV lists by independent developers. |

The three steps below are written for a coding assistant: the computer needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as
the TV, with a shell on it, plus Python 3, a JDK from 17 through 22, and Android SDK platform 34
with build-tools 34 (the assistant builds the launcher there).
Without an assistant, [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand)
is the same job, run by you, and it has the install commands.

Any of these work: Claude Code (on [0G Private Computer](https://pc.0g.ai/?utm_source=cleanyourtv&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme) or an [Anthropic plan](https://claude.com/pricing)), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) or [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli).

| Where | What to do |
|---|---|
| **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. |
| **2. On your computer** | Clone the repo and open that folder in your assistant (`git clone https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv`), then paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) and fill in your TV model. |
| **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, the dock size and app order, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. |

Cloning matters: the assistant reuses this repo's `tools/disable.sh` and `launcher/build-and-install.sh`
instead of writing its own, and that is where the backup, the Home guard and the restore record live.

The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with
screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes.

## What you get

A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way:

| Part | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| **A pitch-black home** | A dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. |
| **A top shelf** | Names the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. |
| **The rest of your apps in a grid** | Slides up when you press Down. |
| **One floating glass highlight** | Springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. |
| **Three frosted buttons** | Inputs (HDMI ports under the names you gave them in the TV's settings, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. |
| **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** | In [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit), and a matching Clock screensaver. Set `show_stats` in config or a theme for one line under the clock: CPU, free memory and free storage. It stays off unless you turn it on, and it refreshes only while Home is on screen. |
| **Themes and module cards** | Themes change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and module cards let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. |

And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics
phoning home, no apps you never asked for.

## What's changed

- Added a warning to `/schedule` when a new cloud scheduled task gets connectors you did not ask for, with how to remove them
- Added a check that asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email address to the network
- Added `onFailure: "block"` for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run
- Added a notice in Claude Desktop's Code tab when your organization's remote managed settings haven't loaded for the session, and another once they do
- Added a notice when auto mode's check has no answer for a subagent's tool call, which used to leave nothing in the main view
- Added `anthropic.plan`, `anthropic.seat_type`, `anthropic.provider` and `anthropic.custom_base_url` to OTel metrics, events and spans
- Added a cost report to the Claude apps gateway admin API, `GET /v1/organizations/analytics/cost`, for reading past spend over a date range in total, per developer, per day or per IdP group
- Added a daily record of each developer's IdP groups on Claude apps gateways with `admin:` set, kept for `admin.identity_retention_days`, which the cost report groups by
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NESTED_SESSION_ID`: set it to `1` on a self-hosted runner to have `claude -p` run inside a session use that session's ID and transcript, as in earlier versions
- Fixed project and local MCP servers disconnecting after the first turn in some Claude desktop sessions
- Fixed auto mode failing every turn when an LLM gateway set as the base URL answers 403 or 422 to its server-side safety check (a 403 with an apiKeyHelper is unchanged)
- Fixed `claude auth status` exiting before a slow token refresh was saved, which could sign you out on the next run
- Fixed a project's `effortLevel` setting being ignored by sessions that an app starts ahead of time and then opens in the project, such as new sessions in the desktop app's Code tab
- Fixed `claude --from-pr` reporting "No conversations found" in projects with many sessions when the linked session was older than the first page
- Fixed the second of two simultaneous permission prompts showing no file path or command on claude.ai and the mobile apps
- Fixed Remote Control and SDK hosts offering "don't ask again" on a mod's tool calls
- Fixed session titles being lost in cloud and SDK sessions when a new message or Stop arrived while the title was generating
- Fixed self-paced `/loop` wakeups sometimes not being scheduled when Claude left a field out of its request
- Fixed auto mode in cloud sessions stopping for approval when the Artifact tool uploaded, wrote to a database or saved a file through the outputs folder
- Fixed skills synced from claude.ai being lost or downloaded again every ten minutes when they can't be written to disk
- Fixed `/schedule` leaving a cloud scheduled task's next run time and link out of its results after creating or updating it
- Fixed screen readers speaking a running subagent's elapsed time and token count on ever

releases.name: sdk-v1.4.0
releases.body:
### Features

* **api:** add GA methods for analytics, spend limits and RBAC
* **api:** add named beta types for unified metrics and RBAC delete responses
* **api:** add shared analytics order and increase request actor types
* **api:** add tool_use_limit_reached_error and compaction_limit_reached_error session error types
* **api:** add types for analytics group_by and spend limit period filters
* **api:** add user_profile_id to External Keys and Workspaces


### Bug Fixes

* **api:** make spend_limit nullable in the spend limit increase request approve response
* **api:** require always-sent analytics fields and drop the unused project product field


### Chores

* **ci:** install only the headless Chromium shell in the browser ecosystem tests
* **ci:** remove unused build upload steps
* **docs:** clarify the Slack channel id description
* **docs:** clarify what disabling the Compliance API stops
* **docs:** clarify what the capability_access_all role action grants
* **docs:** link Dreams model fields to the supported models section
* **docs:** update example user ID in Admin API examples
* **internal:** add a section for each repository's own review rules
* **internal:** plainer wording in worker comments
* **internal:** type-check the published declarations of every subpackage

### Documentation

* add a description to the AnthropicBeta type
* **examples:** keep the message threads example valid on Sonnet 5.5
* **examples:** use current model IDs
* **readme:** point to the docs site for documentation

releases.body:
### Minor Changes

- [#16660](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16660) [`34f34b3`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/34f34b3dbf9ae70218115a4067f66565d184ed5e) Thanks [@punkeel](https://github.com/punkeel)! - Allow opting into zstd compression for Wrangler-built container image layers with `WRANGLER_CONTAINER_IMAGE_COMPRESSION=zstd`.

### Patch Changes

- [#16670](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16670) [`b14b9dc`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/b14b9dcc360d1e05bb29a87287624603c2c60815) Thanks [@dependabot](https://github.com/apps/dependabot)! - Update `DEFAULT_COMPAT_DATE` to 2026-11-03

  Use the bundled workerd release's compatibility date by default when scaffolding new projects or when no compatibility date is configured.

- [#16011](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16011) [`44d1ee4`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/44d1ee439c0a077f2fed4d86e35a4edf46b51f74) Thanks [@wra-sol](https://github.com/wra-sol)! - Offer to delete a Worker's Container applications when running `wrangler delete`

  Previously, `wrangler delete` removed only the Worker, leaving the Container applications that `wrangler deploy` created for it running and billing. It now offers to delete them as well. With `--force`, or in CI and other non-interactive contexts, it lists them instead so they can be removed with `wrangler containers delete <id>`.

- [#16670](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16670) [`b14b9dc`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/b14b9dcc360d1e05bb29a87287624603c2c60815) Thanks [@dependabot](https://github.com/apps/dependabot)! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

  - miniflare@5.20261103.0-beta

## Release Notes

Released on 2026-11-03.

### Preview features

- Add `--output-version` to `uv workspace metadata` for requesting a specific schema version ([#22958](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22958))
- Report aliased OSV records as a single vulnerability in `uv audit` ([#22990](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22990))

### Bug fixes

- Treat workspace member paths added by `uv init` or `uv add` as literals instead of glob patterns ([#23008](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23008))
- Prevent uv's Windows trampolines from closing handles they did not inherit ([#22977](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22977))
- Allow `uvx` to run tools with CPython builds whose versions contain local identifiers ([#23013](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23013))
- Generate valid module names when `uv init` creates packaged projects whose names start with a digit ([#23022](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23022))
- Preserve comments around existing inline dependency groups when `uv add` updates a group ([#23017](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23017))
- Allow `uv remove` with an empty inline `tool.uv.sources` table ([#23012](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23012))

### Documentation

- Correct the `cache-keys` inline table example ([#22984](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22984))

## Install uv 0.13.7

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.7/uv-installer.sh | sh
```

### Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

```sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.7/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"
```
